question.leadin: Identify some people in the history of a certain empire that was neither holy nor Roman.
question.text: This Holy Roman Emperor, third of the Salian dynasty, was involved in the Investiture Controversy with the Papacy and stood in the snow for three days begging for forgiveness.
question.clue: This ruler, who was assassinated by the zealot Francois Ravaillac, was married to Marie de Medici, who later led the "Day of the Dupes" against Cardinal Richelieu.

swap.text: Fredrick Barborossa occupied this position, which was elected to be the catholic ruler of the German principalities. Other holders of this position were Charles V and Otto the Great.
swap.clue: The Treaty of Pressburg invalidated this office after the battle of Austerlitz in 1806, and it was selected by seven electors after the 1356 Golden Bull.

question.leadin: Name some leaders associated with the 3rd Crusade.
question.text: This German Holy Roman Emperor attempted to lead an army of 150,000 into the Holy Land, however, he drowned when his horse slipped while crossing the Saleph River.
question.clue: He attempted to suppress the revolt of the Lombard League twice; the second time, the head of the Guelphs, Henry the Lion, refused to assist him.

swap.leadin: One monarch with this name legendarily raised several children without human interaction in an attempt to find a universal natural language.
swap.text: Give this regnal name of the victor of the Sixth Crusade. An earlier Holy Roman Emperor with this name was defeated at Legnano [le-NYA-no] by the Lombard League.
swap.clue: That person, the author of the Constitutions of Melfi, was excommunicated four times, including during their successful negotiation of the return of Jerusalem.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Battle of Wimpfen.
question.text: The attackers in the Battle of Wimpfen belonged to this organization that opposed the Protestant Union. A French organization founded by Henry, Duke of Guise was also named this two-word phrase.
question.clue: Another group of this name opposed King Henry III and took power during the Day of the Barricades.

swap.text: After the Council of Constance, these wars were fought against Bohemians who followed the teachings of a namesake Czech reformer. Until his death, Jan Zizka led the radical Taborite faction to victories in these wars.
swap.clue: Raids called "beautiful rides" were conducted by Prokop the Great in this conflict, which ended at the Battle of Lipany where the Utraquists defeated the Taborites.

question.leadin: FTPE, name some rulers of the Holy Roman Empire.
question.text: The first Emperor of the Saxon dynasty, this man resurrected the Empire from the ashes of the Carolingians after his victory at Lechfeld over the Magyars.
question.answerHtml: Otto I the Great (need one or the other)
question.clue: After further rebellions by his son Ludolph and by Conrad the Red, this man terminated their powers at the Imperial Diet of Auerstadt.

swap.leadin: This interbred family met a sad end when its last male heirs proved infertile and mentally challenged after 500 years of marrying their own cousins.
swap.text: Name this royal house, whose most famous member was Holy Roman Emperor Charles V of Spain.
swap.answer: the House of Habsburg or Hapsburg

question.text: In 1469, Corvinus also was elected king of this kingdom in the modern Czech Republic. After a namesake war, Corvinus agreed to limit his rule of this kingdom to Moravia, Silesia, and Lusatia.
question.clue: Holy Roman Emperor Matthias took control of this region after imprisoning his ailing brother, Rudolf II ("the-second").

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about some important Conrads.
swap.text: Conrad III was the first member of this royal house, which originated in the Duchy of Swabia, to rule as King of Germany. Things didn't really get going until the reign of Conrad's successor, Frederick Barbarossa.
swap.clue: That founder suppressed the Commune of Rome and its leader Arnold of Brescia, beat the Seljuks at the battle of Iconium, and held the Diet of Roncaglia after losing at Legnano to the Lombard League.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Lion of the north, Gustavus Adolphus.
question.text: At Lutzen, Gustavus' forces triumphed, but he died battling this Catholic general. This Bohemian was the supreme commander for the Hapsburg forces, but eventually was assassinated before he could defect to the Protestants.
question.clue: At Lutzen, Swedish forces defeated this capable Bohemian general. Emperor Ferdinand II had this man killed when he seemed likely to defect to the Protestant side.

swap.text: After his excommunication during the investiture controversy, Emperor Henry IV made a pilgrimage to this castle to beg for readmission to the church. Henry allegedly waited at the gate of this castle for three days in the snow.
swap.clue: The most famous visitor to this city fasted for three days outside its castle during a blizzard to beg for forgiveness from Pope Gregory VII.

question.leadin: As a result of declarations made at this event, Jacob Poost was arrested, while Jan van Essen and Hendrik Vos were burnt at the stake.
question.text: Name this event condemning a man who defended his views from Leo X's ("the tenthʼs") bull Exsurge domine. Johann Eck presided over this event, during which its central participant may have said "Here I stand, I cannot do otherwise."
question.clue: One prominent participant in this meeting had to hide at the Wartburg at its conclusion.

swap.text: had attempted to announce the rights he intended to enforce at this 1158 meeting near . He also hoped to restore the earlier suzerainty via the appointment of imperial officials.
swap.clue: This 1158 meeting which promised thirty thousand pounds of silver per year on top of the fodrum tax.

question.text: This Duke of Saxony was father of Otto the Great. This man allegedly gained his epithet after he received word that he was crowned king while he was mending his bird nets.
question.answerHtml: Henry the Fowler [Heinrich der Finkler; Heinrich der Vogler; prompt on partial answer]
question.clue: His wife accompanied him on his campaigns building monasteries, one of which was their burial site of Quedlinburg.

swap.text: Guelph-Ghibelline rivalries spread even further as a result of this campaign, which was initiated by Frederick II without any backing from Pope Gregory IX. This campaign succeeded diplomatically despite Frederick's quarrels with the House of Ibelin, and produced a ten-year treaty with little bloodshed.
swap.clue: While this crusade was getting underway, the death of al-Mu'azzzam, the governor of Damascus, prompted French crusaders to fortify the island of Qal'at al-Bahr.

question.leadin: The foremost early leader of this faction was Jacob of Mies, who preached at the University of Prague that the laity should receive the Eucharist in both bread and wine.
question.text: Name this moderate faction that maintained amicable relations with the Roman Catholic Church, and emerged victorious over their rivals at the Battle of Lipany during the Hussite Wars.
question.clue: The radical Taborites were opposed by this more moderate Hussite faction, who eventually broke with their brethren and fought on the side of the Catholics.

swap.leadin: John of Bohemia, of Crecy fame, originally gave Charles IV this name, but Charles renamed himself in honor of Charles the Fair of France.
swap.text: Give this name of several rulers of Prague, like Charles' Nepomuk-killing son. A beloved duke of this name was murdered by his not-so-good brother, Boleslaus the Cruel.
swap.clue: This name was borne by the protege of Saint Ludmila who was killed after refusing to fight Henry the Fowler.

question.text: One of Boulanger's first notable acts was as the Minister of War, where he reversed a policy prohibiting soldiers from possessing these items. They were notably forbidden to the boyars by Peter the Great, and a "hater" of one of these was the subject of Julian the Apostate's diatribe Misopogon.
question.clue: Paul the Deacon wrote a history of people named for these things.

swap.text: Bathory's husband bought the Castle of Csejte from this Holy Roman Emperor. This prominent patron of the arts issued a letter of toleration for Czech Protestants and was deposed by his brother Matthias, after which Bathory was tortured and imprisoned.
swap.clue: This monarch wrote the Letter of Majesty to the Estates of Bohemia, offering religious toleration in exchange for staying on as their sovereign, after being supplanted by his brother Matthias as ruler of Bohemia.
